literal: As Wucheng grew gravely ill, he and Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and others alike received the final testament; Dingyuan was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: As Wucheng sickened toward death, he entrusted the final testament to Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and others alike — and made Dingyuan minister of works.

literal: When Prince of Zhao Commandery memorialized to dismiss He Shikai, Dingyuan joined the plot — then accepted He Shikai's bribe, bringing calamity upon the prince; such was his greed and baseness.
idiomatic: When Prince of Zhao Commandery moved to dismiss He Shikai, Dingyuan joined the plot — then took He Shikai's bribe and brought ruin on the prince. Such was his greed.

literal: Soon he was removed and made Governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: Soon he was made governor of Ying Province.

literal: Earlier, Dingyuan's younger brother Jilue had a performing concubine; Mutipo asked for her, and Dingyuan refused.
idiomatic: Earlier, Dingyuan's brother Jilue had a performing concubine. Mutipo demanded her; Dingyuan refused.

literal: When Gao Sihao rebelled, Mutipo had the director of the Linhuai principality accuse Dingyuan of secretly communicating with Sihao.
idiomatic: When Gao Sihao rose in rebellion, Mutipo had the Linhuai principality's director accuse Dingyuan of secret dealings with Sihao.

literal: The Later Lord ordered Duan Chang, holder of opening-establishment honors, to lead three thousand cavalry in a surprise strike, and sent Attendant Censor Zhao Xiutong to the province to impeach Dingyuan on charges of embezzlement.
idiomatic: The Later Lord ordered Duan Chang, who held opening-establishment honors, to lead three thousand cavalry in a surprise raid, and sent attendant censor Zhao Xiutong to the province to impeach Dingyuan for embezzlement.

literal: Dingyuan suspected a trap and hanged himself.
idiomatic: Dingyuan sensed a trap and hanged himself.

literal: Later he followed Shenwu in raising troops, defeated the Four Hus at Hanling, was enfeoffed Duke of Guangping County, and soon advanced to commandery duke.
idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising arms, routed the Four Hus at Hanling, was enfeoffed duke of Guangping County, and soon advanced to commandery duke.

literal: At the Battle of Heyin the other generals won great victories — only Gan's troops retreated.
idiomatic: At Heyin the other generals won great victories — only Gan's troops fell back.

literal: Shenwu, considering his past merit, did not punish or dismiss him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, weighing his old service, did not punish or dismiss him.

literal: Soon he was made Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: Soon he was made grand preceptor and grand tutor.

literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled at Wulao, Shenwu marched against him and made Gan grand commander as vanguard.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled at Wulao, Gao Huan marched against him and made Gan grand commander of the vanguard.

literal: Gan set out without stopping at home; he met Hou Jing and had no time to eat — Jing sent horsemen racing after him with food.
idiomatic: Gan took the road without stopping at home. He met Hou Jing and had no time to eat — Jing sent riders racing after him with provisions.

literal: At that time Emperor Wen personally led troops to Luoyang; his army's appearance was very imposing.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Western Wei had personally led troops to Luoyang — his army's bearing was formidable.

literal: The generals did not wish to cross south; Gan resolved to ford the river.
idiomatic: The generals shrank from crossing south; Gan resolved to ford the river.

literal: Shenwu's main force followed, and they routed the enemy.
idiomatic: Gao Huan's main army came up behind, and they routed the enemy.

literal: He returned and was made Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: He returned and was made governor of Ding Province.

literal: Unskilled in administration, his affairs were often chaotic — yet he kept himself frugal and simple, and the clerks and people did not resent him.
idiomatic: He was no hand at administration, and his office was often in disorder — yet he lived plainly and frugally, and neither clerks nor commoners resented him.

literal: He was transferred to Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: He was made grand preceptor.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, for his merit as one of the founding ministers of the Tianping era, he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and made Grand Minister.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, for his merit among the Tianping founding ministers, he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and made grand minister.

literal: Gan married Shenwu's sister, Princess of Leling — as kin by marriage, he was treated with special favor.
idiomatic: Gan married Gao Huan's sister, Princess of Leling — as kin by marriage, he was treated with singular favor.

literal: From his first service in the rescue of the throne he often commanded the main armies; the weight of his prestige made the other generals defer to him, and he was the sternest and fiercest of them all.
idiomatic: From the first campaigns to rescue the throne he often commanded the main armies. The weight of his prestige bowed the other generals — and of them all he was the sternest, the fiercest.

literal: Once when he visited the capital, Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou indulged in excessive ribaldry at court — none of the nobles could rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him; Xiaoyou was deeply ashamed, and contemporaries praised Gan.
idiomatic: Once at the capital, Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou carried on with excessive ribaldry at court — and none of the nobles dared rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him. Xiaoyou was deeply shamed; men praised Gan for it.

literal: He died. Posthumously he was granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe and Grand Minister rank, given an imperial carriage; posthumous name Jinglie.
idiomatic: He died. Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe and grand minister rank, given an imperial carriage — posthumous name Jinglie.

literal: Gan could not read; to sign his name he drew the character gan upside down — people called it "piercing the awl."
idiomatic: Gan could not read. To sign his name he drew the character for Gan upside down — people called it "piercing the awl."

literal: There was also the warrior Wang Zhou, who signed by writing the inner part ji first and then completing the outer strokes — not until their descendants did either family learn to read.
idiomatic: There was also the warrior Wang Zhou, who signed by writing the inner strokes of "ji" first and only then completing the character — not until their descendants did either family learn to read.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, Gan was granted posthumous sacrifice in Shenwu's temple hall.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian, Gan was granted posthumous sacrifice in Gao Huan's temple hall.

literal: His son Jingfu rose to rank equal to the three excellencies and died.
idiomatic: His son Jingfu rose to rank equal to the three excellencies and died.

literal: His son Shiwen succeeded him.
idiomatic: His son Shiwen succeeded him.

literal: Shiwen was solitary and upright by nature; even nearest kin and neighbors he would not treat familiarly.
idiomatic: Shiwen was solitary and upright by nature — even nearest kin and neighbors he would not treat familiarly.

literal: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and served as Commander of the Guard Army.
idiomatic: Under Qi he inherited the title Prince of Zhangwu Commandery and served as commander of the guard army.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, many gentry of Shandong came out to welcome the conquerors — Shiwen alone shut his gates and held himself apart.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, the gentry of Shandong poured out to welcome the conquerors — Shiwen alone shut his gates and held himself apart.

literal: The emperor admired this and made him holder of opening-establishment honors equal to the three excellencies and Governor of Sui Province.
idiomatic: The emperor admired this and made him holder of opening-establishment honors equal to the three excellencies, and governor of Sui Province.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was additionally granted supreme opening-establishment honors and enfeoffed Viscount of Hubo County.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was additionally granted supreme opening-establishment honors and enfeoffed viscount of Hubo County.

literal: Soon he was made Governor of Bei Province.
idiomatic: Soon he was made governor of Bei Province.

literal: By nature austere and frugal, he took no official stipend; his household had no surplus wealth.
idiomatic: By nature austere and frugal, he took no official stipend — his household held no surplus.

literal: Once his son ate cakes from the official kitchen; Shiwen had him shackled in prison for days, beaten two hundred strokes, and sent back to the capital on foot — not one servant dared leave the house.
idiomatic: Once his son ate cakes from the official kitchen. Shiwen had him shackled in prison for days, beaten two hundred strokes, and sent back to the capital on foot — not one servant dared leave the house.

literal: Salt and vegetables he bought had to come from outside the jurisdiction.
idiomatic: Salt and vegetables he bought had to come from outside his jurisdiction.

literal: Whenever he went out or returned, he sealed and signed his gate — kin and friends ceased to visit; congratulations and condolences alike went unacknowledged.
idiomatic: Whenever he went out or returned, he sealed and signed his gate. Kin and friends ceased to visit; congratulations and condolences alike went unacknowledged.

literal: His laws were stern; officials and people submitted; no one picked up lost goods on the road.
idiomatic: His laws were stern; officials and people submitted. Lost goods lay untouched on the road.

literal: For the slightest fault he would twist the law to destroy a man.
idiomatic: For the slightest fault he would twist the law to destroy a man.

literal: Once when he came to court, he encountered the emperor granting the high officials entry to the left treasury to take whatever they wished.
idiomatic: Once at court he encountered the emperor granting the high officials entry to the left treasury — take whatever you will.

literal: Everyone took the heaviest loads; Shiwen alone held one bolt of silk in his mouth and one in each hand.
idiomatic: Everyone took the heaviest loads. Shiwen alone held one bolt of silk in his mouth and one in each hand.

literal: The emperor asked why; Shiwen said, "My mouth and hands are both full — I require nothing else.
idiomatic: The emperor asked why. Shiwen said, "My mouth and hands are both full — I require nothing else.

literal: " The emperor marveled and separately sent him gifts.
idiomatic: " The emperor marveled and sent him separate gifts.

literal: When Shiwen reached his province, he rooted out corrupt officials — embezzling even a foot of cloth or a pint of grain earned no mercy. A thousand men were reported and all were sent to garrison duty in Lingnan.
idiomatic: At his province Shiwen rooted out corrupt officials — embezzling even a foot of cloth or a pint of grain earned no mercy. A thousand men were reported up; all were sent to garrison Lingnan.

literal: Kin escorted them weeping; their cries filled the province.
idiomatic: Kin escorted them weeping — their cries filled the province.

literal: Reaching Lingnan, eight or nine in ten died of miasma and pestilence — parents, wives, and children wept only for Shiwen.
idiomatic: Reaching Lingnan, eight or nine in ten died of miasma and pestilence — and parents, wives, and children wept only for Shiwen.

literal: Hearing this, Shiwen had them seized and beaten until the whips piled up before him — and the weeping grew louder.
idiomatic: Hearing this, Shiwen had them seized and beaten until the whips piled before him — and the weeping only grew louder.

literal: Vice Director Wei Kun of Jingzhao and Magistrate of Qinghe Zhao Da of Hedong were both harsh; only the Chief Clerk governed with kindness. People said: "The governor's policy is a rakshasa's; the vice director glares like a viper; the chief clerk judges with a smile; Qinghe's magistrate devours men alive.
idiomatic: Vice director Wei Kun of Jingzhao and magistrate of Qinghe Zhao Da of Hedong were both harsh; only the chief clerk governed with kindness. People said, "The governor's policy is a rakshasa's; the vice director glares like a viper; the chief clerk judges with a smile; Qinghe's magistrate devours men alive.

literal: " The emperor heard and sighed: "Shiwen is more savage than a wild beast.
idiomatic: " The emperor heard and sighed, "Shiwen is more savage than a wild beast.

literal: " In the end he was dismissed for it.
idiomatic: " In the end he was dismissed.

literal: Before long he was made Chief Clerk of Yong Province. He told people: "My laws have always been severe; I cannot court the mighty. I suppose I will die in this post.
idiomatic: Before long he was made chief clerk of Yong Province. He told people, "My laws have always been severe; I cannot court the mighty. I suppose I will die in this post.

literal: " When he took up the post he enforced the law with rigor, fearing no noble kin; not one guest dared come to his door.
idiomatic: " When he took up the post he enforced the law without fear of noble kin — not one guest dared come to his door.

literal: Many nursed resentment against him.
idiomatic: Many nursed resentment against him.

literal: Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Duke of Xue Changsun Lan.
idiomatic: Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful. After Qi's fall she was given to Duke of Xue Changsun Lan.

literal: Lan's wife Lady Zheng, jealous, slandered her to Empress Wenxian; the empress ordered Lan to separate from her.
idiomatic: Lan's wife Lady Zheng, jealous, slandered her to Empress Wenxian — and the empress ordered Lan to cast her off.

literal: Shiwen was shamed and refused to meet with her.
idiomatic: Shiwen was shamed and refused to see her.

literal: Later, when Tang Junming, Governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, Shiwen took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
idiomatic: Later, when Tang Junming, governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, Shiwen took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.

literal: Shiwen was unyielding by nature; after a few days in prison he died of rage and indignation. His household had no surplus; three sons went hungry morning and evening — neither kin nor friends would support them.
idiomatic: Shiwen was unyielding by nature. After a few days in prison he died of rage and indignation. His household held nothing spare; three sons went hungry morning and evening — neither kin nor friends would support them.

literal: Han Gui, courtesy name Bainian, was a native of Dina in Tai'an.
idiomatic: Han Gui, courtesy name Bainian, was a native of Dina in Tai'an.

literal: From youth he had resolution and integrity; deep and reserved, he never showed pleasure or anger on his face.
idiomatic: From youth he had resolution and integrity — deep and reserved, he never showed pleasure or anger on his face.

literal: When Shenwu held Jin Province, he recruited Gui as garrison commander of the walled city.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan held Jin Province, he recruited Gui as garrison commander of the walled city.

literal: When troops were raised at Xindu, Gui supported the great plan.
idiomatic: When arms were raised at Xindu, Gui supported the great plan.

literal: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and fought at Hanling; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pingchang County.
idiomatic: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and fought at Hanling — and was enfeoffed marquis of Pingchang County.

literal: He continued to command the center army and followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge.
idiomatic: He continued to command the center army and followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge.

literal: He was twice transferred and made Governor of Tai Province.
idiomatic: He was made governor of Tai Province.

literal: He won great peace on the frontier.
idiomatic: He won deep peace on the frontier.

literal: When Shenwu inspected Tai Province and wished to transfer Gui away, he granted each household in the city two bolts of silk and cloth apiece.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan inspected Tai Province and wished to transfer Gui away, he granted each household in the city two bolts of silk and cloth.

literal: Seven thousand households led by Tian Zhao all declined the gift and begged only that Gui remain.
idiomatic: Seven thousand households led by Tian Zhao declined the gift and begged only that Gui remain.

literal: Shenwu praised and sighed with admiration — and kept him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan praised and sighed with admiration — and kept him.

literal: Repeatedly for military merit he was advanced to Duke of Ande Commandery.
idiomatic: Again and again for military merit he was advanced to duke of Ande Commandery.

literal: Made Governor of Ying Province, he accumulated wealth in the province; the censorate impeached him and stripped his office and rank.
idiomatic: Made governor of Ying Province, he amassed wealth in office — the censorate impeached him and stripped his office and rank.

literal: Before long his ducal title of Ande was restored.
idiomatic: Before long his ducal title of Ande was restored.

literal: He rose through the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Education.
idiomatic: He rose through director of the secretariat and minister of education.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was enfeoffed Prince of Ande Commandery.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he was enfeoffed Prince of Ande Commandery.

literal: Shenwu took Gui's younger sister as consort; she bore Prince Huan of Shangdang. Again through merit Gui rose to the highest offices of state.
idiomatic: Gao Huan took Gui's younger sister as consort; she bore Prince Huan of Shangdang. Again through merit Gui rose to the highest offices of state.

literal: He always conducted himself with humility and deference, never lording his wealth and rank over others.
idiomatic: He always conducted himself with humility — never lording his wealth and rank over others.

literal: Later he was made Grand Marshal; campaigning against the Rouran with Wenxuan, he died suddenly of illness in camp.
idiomatic: Later he was made grand marshal. Campaigning against the Rouran with Wenxuan, he died suddenly of illness in camp.

literal: Posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Minister and Grand Preceptor; posthumous name Suwu.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand minister and grand preceptor — posthumous name Suwu.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian he was granted posthumous sacrifice in Wenxiang's temple hall.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian he was granted posthumous sacrifice in Wenxiang's temple hall.

literal: His son Jinming succeeded him.
idiomatic: His son Jinming succeeded him.

literal: During Tiantong his title was changed to Prince of Donglai.
idiomatic: During Tiantong his title was changed to Prince of Donglai.

literal: Jinming had a chivalrous spirit; among the sons of meritorious nobles he was most devoted to learning.
idiomatic: Jinming had a chivalrous spirit — among the sons of meritorious nobles he was most devoted to learning.

literal: He loved wine and lived without restraint, gathering guests — a single feast often cost ten thousand cash, and he still complained it was too frugal.
idiomatic: He loved wine and lived without restraint, gathering guests — a single feast often cost ten thousand cash, and he still complained it was too spare.

literal: Whenever the court offered him a lofty post, he declined on grounds of illness.
idiomatic: Whenever the court offered him a lofty post, he declined on grounds of illness.

literal: He told people: "A useless man drinking fine wine and sealing famous vistas — how could I go back to being a clerk pawing over old papers?
idiomatic: He told people, "A useless man drinking fine wine and sealing famous vistas — how could I go back to being a clerk pawing over old papers?

literal: " At the end of Wuping he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; after little more than a hundred days he resigned on grounds of illness.
idiomatic: " At the end of Wuping he was made left vice director of the Masters of Writing — after little more than a hundred days he resigned on grounds of illness.

literal: Pan Le, courtesy name Xianggui, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.
idiomatic: Pan Le, courtesy name Xianggui, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.

literal: Originally a great clan of Guangzong, in Wei times they were posted to guard the northern frontier and settled there.
idiomatic: Originally a great clan of Guangzong — in Wei times they were posted to guard the northern frontier and settled there.

literal: His father Yong had technical skills and inherited the barony of Guangzong.
idiomatic: His father Yong had technical skills and inherited the barony of Guangzong.

literal: When Le was born a sparrow alighted on his mother's left shoulder; diviners all said it was a sign of wealth and rank — hence the name Xianggui, later adopted as his courtesy name.
idiomatic: When Le was born a sparrow alighted on his mother's left shoulder. Diviners all said it was a sign of wealth and rank — hence the name Xianggui, later adopted as his courtesy name.

literal: When he grew up he was generous, broad-minded, and possessed of courage and strategy.
idiomatic: When he grew up he was generous and broad-minded, possessed of courage and strategy.

literal: At first he joined Ge Rong and was made Prince of Jingzhao — he was nineteen.
idiomatic: At first he joined Ge Rong and was made Prince of Jingzhao — he was nineteen.

literal: When Rong was defeated he followed Erzhu Rong, served as a separate commander against Yuan Hao, and for merit was enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng County.
idiomatic: When Rong was defeated he followed Erzhu Rong, served as a separate commander against Yuan Hao, and for merit was enfeoffed baron of Fucheng County.

literal: When Shenwu went out to hold Jin Province, he recruited Le as garrison general of the walled city.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan went out to hold Jin Province, he recruited Le as garrison general of the walled city.

literal: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and was advanced to Earl of Guangzong County.
idiomatic: He followed in the defeat of Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and was advanced to earl of Guangzong County.

literal: Repeatedly for military merit he was made Governor of Eastern Yong Province.
idiomatic: Again and again for military merit he was made governor of Eastern Yong Province.

literal: Shenwu once debated abolishing the province; Le argued that Eastern Yong lay between mountains and rivers, bordered Hu and Shu territories, and occupied a strategically vital junction — it could not be abandoned. The province remained as before.
idiomatic: Gao Huan once debated abolishing the province. Le argued that Eastern Yong lay between mountains and rivers, bordered Hu and Shu, and occupied a strategically vital junction — it could not be abandoned. The province remained as before.

literal: Later, after defeating Zhou troops at Heyin, there was debate over pursuit — those willing to pursue stood west, the unwilling east. Only Le and Liu Feng stood on the west.
idiomatic: Later, after defeating Zhou troops at Heyin, there was debate over pursuit — those willing to pursue stood west, the unwilling east. Only Le and Liu Feng stood on the west.
